content: The objective of the TNT trial was to evaluate the effectiveness of two different daily doses of atorvastatin, 10 mg and 80 mg, in patients with stable coronary artery disease (CAD) who had baseline LDL cholesterol levels ranging from 130 mg/dL to 250 mg/dL. The TNT trial was a randomized clinical study that included 10,001 patients diagnosed with stable coronary artery disease. Participants were assigned to receive either 80 mg or 10 mg of atorvastatin daily. The median follow-up period for the study was 4.9 years. The results demonstrated that patients receiving the higher dose of atorvastatin (80 mg) achieved significantly lower mean serum LDL cholesterol levels compared to those on the lower dose (77 mg/dL vs. 101 mg/dL). Additionally, the high-dose group experienced a significant reduction in the incidence of the primary composite endpoint (8.7% vs. 10.9%). However, there was no observed reduction in all-cause mortality with the higher dose. While the higher dose of atorvastatin reduced mortality related to cardiac events, it was associated with an increased mortality rate from non-cardiovascular causes. In conclusion, the use of an 80-mg dose of atorvastatin in patients with stable coronary artery disease is considered safe and cost-effective. It provides an additional reduction in coronary events compared to the lower dose, despite the noted increase in non-cardiovascular mortality.
